name: Binnui
overview: Binnui was a male descendant of Pahath-moab noted in the book of Ezra. He is specifically identified as one who had married a foreign wife, a significant detail in the post-exilic community's efforts to maintain covenant purity. No tribe or additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Binnui means "son" in Hebrew. It is a proper name mentioned in Ezra 10:30, and there is no indication that it was given by God or carries a special title beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Binnui as a descendant of Pahath-moab. Beyond this lineage, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text provided.
scriptureSignificance: Binnui's significance lies in his association with the issue of intermarriage among the returned exiles, as he is listed among those who had taken foreign wives. This reflects the challenges faced by the post-exilic community in upholding the covenantal standards set by God. His mention underscores the broader narrative of repentance and reform found in Ezra 10.
